hypothesis: If the claim holds, boys' and girls' stature velocity curves will have a similar shape, differing mainly in timing, with girls' adolescent acceleration earlier.
pass_criterion: After shifting the girls' curve in time, its correlation with the boys' velocity curve is >= 0.9; the girls' peak velocity age is 1.0-3.0 years earlier than the boys'; the unshifted correlation is lower than the shifted one.
fail_criterion: The peak ages differ by < 0.5 years or girls are later, or the shifted correlation is < 0.7.
interpretation: 'Amplitude' is the peak velocity and 'phase' is the age of onset and peak. Velocity is estimated by differencing mean measured stature by single year of age and sex, using cross-sectional data.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: age, RIAGENDR (sex), BMXHT (measured stature) and survey weights, which give weighted mean stature by age and sex.
